purpose: Separate preregistered test of whether independently named tools are suitable, integrable and auditable, not mere requirement coverage. Original 11-criterion rubric remains binding and unchanged.

critical_requirements.pass: Each critical operation has at least one real executable engine with plausible API, correct operational mode, clear required inputs and outputs, and an honest limitation; no static approximation presented as proof of unmodeled phenomena.

Each essential tool is suitable for the actual 3-phase distribution problem, six-scenario planning, crew scheduling, and needed protection/safety checks, or explicitly delegates missing functions to a capable named tool; no ungrounded SLA guarantee.

Candidate solver, validators, graph/crew engines and audit workflow exchange defined compatible artifacts and units with no uncovered mandatory operation, and infeasibility flows back into remediation; unresolved joins are marked as blockers.
Every high-consequence claim has a reproducible verification test, acceptance evidence, explicit rejection conditions, and a distinct independent checker not simply trusting the proposing optimizer.

Distinguishes what is runnable now from what requires missing network/relay/SCADA data, licensing, custom glue or benchmarks; provides a staged low-cost implementation and fallback, not fabricated execution.

other_conditions: No numeric real-world restoration schedule may be invented.
If any original critical criterion C1..C8 fails, stage one fails.
If any appropriateness critical gate A1..A5 fails, stage one fails.
The original historical K2.6 score and trial remain unchanged.
Stage two prohibited absent both gates passing.
